Let's refactor how DiscoverAndRegisterAlways is working right now. 
First, go and check its implementation. What it is doing and why, where is used, and why.
Seconds, follow my specs about how it should work after the refactor.
Third, challenge my solution with possible scenarios I didn't cover until we reach an implementation agreement and only then, write down unit test about how we have decide it has to work and then, very last step, you do the implementation. Delete as many test as you need as we are refactoring. Keep only the realistic testing. Do not over engineer the solution.

My specs:
- DiscoverAndRegisterAlways should first, find all the possible external agents. So, given a PATH it has to create an string array with all the binaries which follow our external agent pattern
- for each binary, we spin a goroutine where we call the info command to get the capabilities, once we get the capabilities on the goroutine it should send back to the waiting channel the wrap agent. This goroutine should run in a context with a timeout very strict, this info command has to be almost instant, make this timeout for now 300ms but I will refine it later.
- if a binary fails loading its capabilities we have to store inside the registy the ready agents to call and the erroer agents that exists but can't be loaded with its error. This should be useful for later on listing current external agent state.

## plugin:entire-engineering:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. - diagnose: Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Reproduce → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test. Use when user says "diagnose this" / "debug this", reports a bug, says something is broken/throwing/failing, or describes a performance regression.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- github-triage: Triage GitHub issues through a label-based state machine. Use when user wants to create an issue, triage issues, review incoming bugs or feature requests, prepare issues for an AFK agent, or manage issue workflow.
- review-pr-feedback: Walk every unresolved review thread on the current branch's PR — fix what is fixable, ask the user about anything ambiguous, then reply on each thread and mark it resolved. Use when the user says "review PR feedback", "go thru the PR comments", "address review comments", or similar.
- ship: Commit, push, and update the PR description or add a comment based on new changes. Use when the user says "ship it", "commit push and update pr", or similar.

For individual phases, use /agent-integration:research, /agent-integration:write-tests, or /agent-integration:implement. Use when the user says "integrate agent", "add agent support", or wants to run the full agent integration pipeline end-to-end.

content.text: Enough context to challenge the spec. Let me put the open decisions to you.

questions.question: Where should the "ready + errored" external agent state live?

options.label: New state in external pkg (Rec.)
options.description: Package-level mutex-guarded map in cmd/entire/cli/agent/external, e.g. external.Discovered() returning ready entries + failed entries with their error. agent.Register stays factories-only, so nothing else in the codebase changes.

options.label: Extend agent registry
options.description: Teach cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go to hold entries that carry an error instead of a factory. Every registry consumer (List, Get, StringList, DetectAll) has to learn about broken entries.

questions.question: Which failures become "errored agents" in the registry vs. silent skips?

options.label: Only info-call failures (Rec.)
options.description: Errored = exec failed, 300ms timeout, bad JSON, protocol mismatch, wrap failure. Silently skipped = glob match is a directory, missing exec bit, name collides with a built-in agent. Those aren't agents at all, so listing them as broken is noise.
options.preview:
errored:  exec failure, timeout,
          invalid JSON, protocol mismatch
skipped:  directory, no +x bit,
          name conflicts with built-in

options.label: Everything unusable is an error
options.description: A non-executable entire-agent-foo or one shadowing a built-in also lands in the registry with an explanatory error, so `entire agent list` can tell the user why their plugin isn't showing up.

questions.question: DiscoverAndRegisterAlways is called up to 4x in one setup flow. On repeat calls?

options.label: Memoize both outcomes (Rec.)
options.description: A binary already recorded — ready or errored — is not re-exec'd for the rest of the process. Today successes are effectively cached (registry lookup) but failures are re-exec'd on every call, costing 300ms each. Trade-off: a transient failure sticks for the process, which is a short-lived CLI.
options.preview:
call 1: exec 3 binaries (1 fails)
call 2..4: 0 execs
total: 3 process spawns

options.label: Retry failures each call
options.description: Only successes are skipped; failed binaries are re-exec'd on every invocation. A flaky binary gets more chances, at up to 300ms per failure per call.

questions.question: DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways (single named binary, used by --summarize-provider / dispatch) currently gets 10s.

options.label: Leave it at 10s (Rec.)
options.description: It's an explicit, one-binary, user-named request where the user is waiting on that specific agent — a slow cold start should work, not fail. Keeps this refactor scoped to the scan path.

options.label: Unify at 300ms
options.description: One timeout constant for every info call. Simpler to reason about, but a cold-start plugin the user explicitly asked for by name would now fail fast instead of loading.

func discoverAndRegister(ctx context.Context) {
	// As above: `ctx` remains the caller's, the derived timeout is named.
	discoveryCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, discoveryTimeout)
	defer cancel()

	pathEnv := os.Getenv("PATH")
	if pathEnv == "" {
		return
	}

	// Collect already-registered names to avoid conflicts.
	registered := make(map[types.AgentName]bool)
	for _, name := range agent.List() {
		registered[name] = true
	}

	seen := make(map[string]bool) // deduplicate binaries across PATH dirs
	for _, dir := range filepath.SplitList(pathEnv) {
		if discoveryCanceled(ctx, discoveryCtx) {
			logging.Debug(ctx, "external agent discovery timed out")
			return
		}

		matches, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(dir, binaryPrefix+"*"))
		if err != nil {
			continue // skip unreadable directories
		}
		for _, binPath := range matches {
			if discoveryCanceled(ctx, discoveryCtx) { ... return }

			name := filepath.Base(binPath)
			if seen[name] { continue }
			seen[name] = true

			cleanName := StripExeExt(name)
			agentName := types.AgentName(strings.TrimPrefix(cleanName, binaryPrefix))
			if registered[agentName] {
				logging.Debug(ctx, "skipping external agent (name conflict with built-in)", ...)
				continue
			}

			registeredAgent, err := registerExternalAgent(discoveryCtx, binPath, agentName)
			if err != nil {
				logging.Debug(ctx, "skipping external agent (registration failed)",
					slog.String("binary", binPath),
					slog.String("agent", string(agentName)),
					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
				continue
			}
			if registeredAgent {
				registered[agentName] = true
			}
		}
	}
}

func registerExternalAgent(ctx context.Context, binPath string, name types.AgentName) (bool, error) {
	finfo, err := statExternalAgent(binPath)
	if err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) { return false, nil }
		return false, fmt.Errorf("inspecting external agent %q binary %q: %w", name, binPath, err)
	}
	if finfo.IsDir() { return false, nil }
	// Check executable bit (on Unix; Windows doesn't set execute bits).
	if runtime.GOOS != osWindows && finfo.Mode()&0o111 == 0 { return false, nil }

	ea, err := New(ctx, binPath)
	if err != nil {
		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); ctxErr != nil {
			return false, fmt.Errorf("loading info for external agent %q from binary %q: %w: %w", name, binPath, ctxErr, err)
		}
		return false, fmt.Errorf("loading info for external agent %q from binary %q: %w", name, binPath, err)
	}

	wrapped, err := Wrap(ea)
	if err != nil {
		return false, fmt.Errorf("wrapping external agent %q from binary %q: %w", name, binPath, err)
	}
	agent.Register(name, func() agent.Agent { return wrapped })

	logging.Debug(ctx, "registered external agent", slog.String("name", string(name)),
		slog.String("type", string(ea.Type())), slog.String("binary", binPath))
	return true, nil
}

content.text: Two genuine problems with the answers I got, which I need to resolve before writing the plan.

questions.question: Error entries can't share the registry's name→factory map: a binary named `entire-agent-claude-code` collides with the working built-in, and `Get`/`DetectAll`/`GetByAgentType` call `factory()` unconditionally (nil factory = panic). How do I extend the registry?

options.label: Sibling map in agent pkg (Rec.)
options.description: registry.go gains a second package-level map keyed by BINARY PATH holding discovery results (ready + failed, each with name, binary, error). Ready agents additionally go into the existing name→factory map. Get/List/StringList/DetectAll keep exactly today's semantics; the new state is read by a new ExternalDiscoveryState() accessor.

options.label: One map, entries carry error
options.description: registry becomes map[AgentName]entry{factory, err}. Every consumer (Get, List, StringList, DetectAll, GetByAgentType, LauncherFor, Default) must be taught to skip error entries, and a conflicting binary either shadows the built-in or is dropped anyway.

questions.question: A binary at `entire-agent-foo` whose info reports `"name": "bar"`. Today it registers under key `foo` while its Name() returns `bar` — silently inconsistent. Under "everything unusable is an error"?

options.label: Leave as-is, out of scope (Rec.)
options.description: Keep registering under the binary-derived name. I can't see the real out-of-tree plugins' info payloads (e.g. entire-agent-roger-roger lives in another repo), so turning this into an error could break working plugins for a cosmetic inconsistency. Note it in the plan as a follow-up.

options.label: Make it an error entry
options.description: info.name must equal the binary suffix, or the agent lands in the registry as errored. Cleaner contract, but any existing plugin with a mismatch stops working the moment this ships.

# Refactor external agent discovery: parallel, strictly-bounded, state-recording

## Context

`external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery.go`) scans `$PATH`
for `entire-agent-*` binaries, execs each one's `info` subcommand, and registers the result in the
agent registry. Three problems with how it works today:

1. **Sequential.** Binaries are exec'd one at a time inside a single 10s budget that is only checked
   *between* binaries. A hung binary is bounded instead by `external.defaultRunTimeout` (30s), so a
   scan can overrun its own 10s cap by ~30s. The two hook call sites
   (`hooks_cmd.go:48`, `hooks_git_cmd.go:177`) wrap it in a 5s context, which a single slow plugin
   can blow through.
2. **Failures vanish.** `discoverAndRegister` returns nothing. Every failure — bad JSON, protocol
   mismatch, non-zero exit, missing exec bit, timeout — goes to `logging.Debug` and the loop moves
   on. A user whose plugin does not appear has no way to find out why.
3. **Name conflicts are silently skipped.** A binary whose derived name matches a built-in is
   dropped with a debug line, so an intentional override of a built-in agent is impossible and
   invisible.

Outcome wanted: discovery that is fast and predictable (all binaries probed in parallel under a
strict per-binary timeout), that records *why* a binary was unusable, that lets an external agent
deliberately take over a built-in name, and that surfaces broken plugins in `entire agent list`.

## Decisions (agreed)

- **Per-binary timeout is 300ms**, a `var` so it is one line to retune later. Applies to the scan
  path *and* to `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways`. The 10s aggregate budget is deleted — with
  parallel probes the wall clock is ~300ms, and the caller's context still caps everything.
- **Everything unusable is an error entry**: exec failure, timeout, invalid JSON, protocol
  mismatch, `Wrap` failure, missing exec bit, glob match that is a directory.
- **An external agent overrides a built-in of the same name**, logged at Info (not Debug) so the
  takeover is always visible. If the overriding external is *broken*, it shadows the built-in and
  the built-in becomes unavailable. That is the user's problem to fix, not something to defend
  against.
- **Memoized per process**: a binary already probed — ready or failed — is not re-exec'd. Keyed by
  binary path. `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` is called up to 4x in one setup flow today.
- **State lives in the agent registry** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go`), not in a new home.
- **`info.name` mismatching the binary suffix stays working** (registers under the binary-derived
  name, as today) and gets a warning log. It is cosmetic: every resolution path in the CLI keys off
  the registry name, never `Agent.Name()`; the mismatch only reaches log attributes and
  `AgentSession.AgentName` (`resume.go:1048`). Turning it into an error would break any
  out-of-tree plugin that already has one.

## Design

### 1. Registry entries carry either a factory or an error

`cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go`, replacing `map[types.AgentName]Factory`:

```go
type entry struct {
    factory Factory // nil when the external binary could not be loaded
    binary  string  // external binaries only; "" for built-ins
    err     error   // non-nil when unusable
}
var registry = make(map[types.AgentName]entry)
```

- `Register(name, factory)` — unchanged signature, stores `entry{factory: factory}`. Built-in
  `init()` registrations are untouched.
- `RegisterExternal(name, binary string, factory Factory)` — stores a usable external, overwriting
  any built-in under that name.
- `RegisterExternalFailure(name, binary string, err error)` — stores `entry{binary, err}`,
  overwriting whatever was there (this is the shadowing case).
- `Get(name)` — entry absent → today's `unknown agent` error; entry with `err != nil` → returns
  that error (wrapped: `external agent %q (%s) is not usable: %w`). Never calls a nil factory.
- `List()`, `StringList()`, `DetectAll()`, `GetByAgentType()`, `LauncherFor()`, `Default()` — skip
  `factory == nil` entries. `List()`/`StringList()` keep meaning "registered and callable", so a
  broken external simply removes the name from the listing while `Get` still explains why.
- `ExternalFailures() []ExternalFailure{Name, Binary, Err}` — sorted by name, for listing.
- `ProbedExternalBinaries() map[string]struct{}` — the memo source, built from entries with a
  non-empty `binary`.
- `ResetExternalsForTesting()` — drops every entry with a non-empty `binary`; tests call it via
  `t.Cleanup` so the process-wide memo does not leak between tests.

### 2. Discovery becomes collect → probe in parallel → register

Rewrite of `discoverAndRegister` in `cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery.go`, in three phases:

**Collect** (`candidates(ctx) []candidate`) — pure filesystem, no exec. Walk
`filepath.SplitList(os.Getenv("PATH"))`, `filepath.Glob(dir + "/entire-agent-*")`, skip unreadable
dirs. Derive the agent name via `StripExeExt` + `TrimPrefix`, and **dedup on the derived agent
name, not the basename** — today's basename dedup lets `foo.exe` and `foo.com` in one dir both
resolve to agent `foo` and silently race (PATHEXT picks one). First PATH dir wins, matching PATH
semantics. Skip anything already in `ProbedExternalBinaries()` (the memo). Returns
`{name, binPath}` pairs.

**Probe** — one goroutine per candidate, each with its own `context.WithTimeout(ctx, infoTimeout)`,
sending a result on a buffered channel. Unbounded fan-out: the realistic candidate count is single
digits, and a cap would only serialize the very case the parallelism is for. Inside the goroutine:
`os.Stat` (directory or missing exec bit on non-Windows → failure result), `New(ctx, binPath)`,
`Wrap(ea)`. Errors keep today's wrapping, so messages stay diagnostic.

**Register** — the calling goroutine drains the channel, sorts results by name for deterministic
ordering, then for each: on success `agent.RegisterExternal` (Info-level log when it overrides an
existing entry; warning log when `info.name` != derived name), on failure
`agent.RegisterExternalFailure`.

A single `ctx.Err() != nil` guard at entry replaces `discoveryCanceled`/`discoveryCtxErr`, which
are deleted. Those two helpers exist only to work around the derived-context-shadowing bug in the
old sequential loop; with each probe owning a context derived from the caller, a cancelled caller
cancels every probe and each error already wraps the context error. `discoveryTimeout` is deleted.

**`discoverAndRegisterNamed`** keeps its `exec.LookPath` shape (it honours PATHEXT) and its
path-separator rejection, switches to `infoTimeout`, records failures the same way, and returns the
error to its caller as it does today. The `statExternalAgent` seam is removed (the real
non-executable/directory tests cover it); `lookPathExternalAgent` stays — `_RejectsPathSeparators`
asserts it is never reached.

### 3. `entire agent list` surfaces broken externals

`runAgentList` in `cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go` currently never discovers externals, so external
agents do not appear there at all. Add `external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways(ctx)` at the top (the
`Always` variant: a listing command should show what is on PATH regardless of the
`external_agents` setting, same reasoning as `runSetupFlow`), then after the existing list print a
section when `agent.ExternalFailures()` is non-empty:

```
Broken external agents:
  ✗ foo  (/usr/local/bin/entire-agent-foo): info: invalid JSON: ...
```

## Tests

Written before the implementation. `cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery_test.go` is largely
rewritten; the existing `setupDiscoveryDir` / `makeInfoJSON` / `enableExternalAgents` /
`mockInfoScript` helpers are reused.

**Kept as-is (still describe real behaviour):** `_EmptyPATH`, `_UnreadableDir`,
`_SkipsWhenDisabled`, `_Deduplication`, `TestIsExternal_*`, the two Windows `.bat` tests, and the
named-variant `_InvalidInfo`, `_MissingHelper`, `_RejectsPathSeparators`, `_CanceledContext`,
`_TimesOutStalledInfo` (retargeted at 300ms).

**Deleted** — they pin mechanisms this refactor removes, or inject through seams that are going
away: `_DeadlineWhileLookingUpMissingHelper`, `_ReportsCallerDeadlineExpiredDuringLookup` plus its
bespoke `stalledPropagationCtx` type, `_HelperDisappearsAfterLookup`, `_StatError`,
`_LookPathError`, `_SkipsNameConflict` (the behaviour it asserts is inverted now),
`_SkipsNonExecutable` and `_SkipsDirectory` (replaced by the failure-recording versions below).

**New:**

| Test | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `_RegistersReadyAgents` | two good binaries in two PATH dirs both registered and callable |
| `_RecordsFailedAgent` | invalid-JSON binary absent from `List()`, present in `ExternalFailures()` with its binary path and a diagnostic error; a good binary in the same scan still registers |
| `_SlowInfoTimesOutWithoutBlockingOthers` | `sleep 60` binary recorded as failed with `context.DeadlineExceeded`, a good binary alongside it registers, whole call well under 2s (proves parallel + isolated) |
| `_ExternalOverridesBuiltIn` | pre-registered built-in factory replaced by a good same-named external; `Get` returns the external |
| `_BrokenExternalShadowsBuiltIn` | pre-registered built-in + broken same-named external → name gone from `List()`/`StringList()`, `Get` returns the external's error, entry in `ExternalFailures()` |
| `_NonExecutableRecordedAsFailure` | mode 0644 match → failure entry, not silent skip |
| `_DirectoryRecordedAsFailure` | directory named `entire-agent-*` → failure entry |
| `_MemoizesReadyAndFailed` | binaries that append to a counter file; two `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` calls produce exactly one exec each, for a good *and* a failing binary |
| `_DedupesOnDerivedAgentName` | same derived name in dir A and dir Z → dir A's binary wins (distinguished by its `info.type`) |
| `_NameMismatchStillRegisters` | `entire-agent-foo` reporting `"name": "bar"` is registered under `foo` and callable |

`cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry_test.go`: `Get` on a failure entry returns the recorded error;
`List`/`StringList` exclude it; `GetByAgentType` and `DetectAll` do not panic on a nil factory.

`cmd/entire/cli/agent_group_test.go`: `runAgentList` output contains a ready external in the normal
list and a broken one under `Broken external agents:` with its reason.

## Docs

- `docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md` — §Discovery is already stale ("runs once during
  CLI initialization"); rewrite it for lazy per-command, parallel, 300ms-per-binary discovery.
  §Error Handling changes from "the binary is skipped" to "recorded as a broken agent and shown by
  `entire agent list`". Document that an external agent overrides a built-in of the same name, and
  that a broken one shadows it. Also add the undocumented `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION` env var to
  §Environment while in there.
- `docs/architecture/external-commands.md` — update the `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` row (~line 267).

## Files touched

- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go` (+ `registry_test.go`)
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery.go` (+ `discovery_test.go`)
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go` (+ `agent_group_test.go`)
- `docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md`, `docs/architecture/external-commands.md`

Deliberately untouched: `external.go` / `capabilities.go` (`New`, `run`, `Wrap` are unchanged), the
`settings.IsExternalAgentsEnabled` gate on `DiscoverAndRegister`, and every call site in
`setup.go` / `explain_summary_provider.go` — the signatures stay identical.

## Verification

1. `mise run test` — unit tests, including the new discovery/registry/list tests.
2. `mise run test:integration` and `mise run test:e2e:canary` — the canary exercises the hook trees
   that call `DiscoverAndRegister` under a 5s context.
3. `mise run fmt && mise run lint` (lint again after fmt if it rewrote anything). Note: use the
   mise-installed golangci-lint binary directly — a stale v1 shadows it on PATH.
4. Manual, in a scratch repo: put three binaries on PATH — one good, one printing garbage, one
   `sleep 60` — and check `entire agent list` shows the good one in the list and the other two under
   `Broken external agents:` with distinct reasons, returning in well under a second. Then add a
   good `entire-agent-claude-code` and confirm the takeover is logged and `entire agent add
   claude-code` drives the external.
5. `time entire agent list` with the `sleep 60` binary present, to confirm the 300ms bound holds.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Turning an `info.name` / binary-suffix mismatch into a hard error.
- Surfacing broken externals in `entire status` / `--json`.
- Retuning `infoTimeout` away from 300ms once real-world cold-start numbers exist (macOS Gatekeeper
  on a first exec of a large Go binary is the case most likely to need it).

   *between* binaries. A hung binary is bounded instead by `external.defaultRunTimeout` (30s), so a
   scan can overrun its own 10s cap by ~30s. The two hook call sites
   (`hooks_cmd.go:48`, `hooks_git_cmd.go:177`) wrap it in a 5s context, which a single slow plugin
   can blow through.
2. **Failures vanish.** `discoverAndRegister` returns nothing. Every failure — bad JSON, protocol
   mismatch, non-zero exit, missing exec bit, timeout — goes to `logging.Debug` and the loop moves
   on. A user whose plugin does not appear has no way to find out why.
3. **Name conflicts are silently skipped.** A binary whose derived name matches a built-in is
   dropped with a debug line, so an intentional override of a built-in agent is impossible and
   invisible.

strict per-binary timeout), that records *why* a binary was unusable, that lets an external agent
deliberately take over a built-in name, and that surfaces broken plugins in `entire agent list`.

- **Everything unusable is an error entry**: exec failure, timeout, invalid JSON, protocol
  mismatch, `Wrap` failure, missing exec bit, glob match that is a directory.
- **An external agent overrides a built-in of the same name**, logged at Info (not Debug) so the
  takeover is always visible. If the overriding external is *broken*, it shadows the built-in and
  the built-in becomes unavailable. That is the user's problem to fix, not something to defend

    binary  string  // external binaries only; "" for built-ins

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page - what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in. Format is not part of this read: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it - a Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title and takes almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first - CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world - its materials, instruments, vernacular - is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the one font host the Artifact CSP admits - link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`); a face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI or it falls back silently. Either way, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject - the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* - most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token - a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Before publishing, scan the stylesheet for any color declared only inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - that is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first - don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme - then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content - tables, code, diagrams - gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly - their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out - a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen - name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it - no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Name the page like a product, not a caption.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it sets the reader's first impression of care. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject - or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which is then the page's name. Stop at the name - a title that carries its own explainer after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it sits beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could sit on any of them fails as a name just as surely as an appended explainer. When a candidate title pairs the name with a generic word - a greeting, a category, a page-type label - the name is the half to keep; a trim that drops the identity and keeps the generic word produces exactly the title that could sit on any page. And the rule removes explainers, it does not impose brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. The one-sentence publish `description` is where the explanation belongs; the gallery shows it right under the title.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number - a pill, a chip, a severity stripe - so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan - a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles - a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world - headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

Refactor plan · entireio/cli

External Agent Discovery Refactor

Rework DiscoverAndRegisterAlways so every entire-agent-* binary on $PATH is probed in parallel under a strict 300 ms budget, and so a binary that cannot be loaded is recorded with its reason instead of disappearing into a debug log.

branch refactor-discover-and-register-external-agents entry point cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery.go call sites 6 production + 1 e2e

Context

Why we are changing this

external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways scans $PATH for entire-agent-* binaries, execs each one's info subcommand, and registers the result in the agent registry. Three problems with how it works today.

  1. 01

    Sequential, with a budget that does not hold

    Binaries are exec'd one at a time inside a single 10 s budget checked only between binaries. A hung binary is bounded instead by external.defaultRunTimeout (30 s), so a scan can overrun its own cap by ~30 s. Both hook call sites wrap the scan in a 5 s context that one slow plugin blows straight through.

  2. 02

    Failures vanish

    discoverAndRegister returns nothing. Bad JSON, protocol mismatch, non-zero exit, missing exec bit, timeout — every one goes to logging.Debug and the loop moves on. A user whose plugin does not appear has no way to find out why.

  3. 03

    Name conflicts are silently skipped

    A binary whose derived name matches a built-in is dropped with a debug line, so deliberately overriding a built-in agent is impossible — and invisible.

Decisions

Agreed behaviour

300 ms per binary
A var, so retuning is one line. Applies to the scan path and to DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways. The 10 s aggregate budget is deleted: with parallel probes the wall clock is ~300 ms and the caller's context is the only cap needed.
Everything unusable is an error entry
Exec failure, timeout, invalid JSON, protocol mismatch, Wrap failure, missing exec bit, and a glob match that turns out to be a directory.
An external overrides a built-in
Same name means the external wins, logged at Info (not Debug) so the takeover is always visible. If the overriding external is broken it shadows the built-in, which then becomes unavailable — the user's problem to fix, not something to defend against.
Memoized per process
A binary already probed — ready or failed — is not re-exec'd. Keyed by binary path. One setup flow calls DiscoverAndRegisterAlways up to four times today.
State lives in the agent registry
cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go, not a new home in the external package.
info.name mismatch keeps working
Registers under the binary-derived name as today, plus a warning log. It is cosmetic: every resolution path keys off the registry name, never Agent.Name() — the mismatch reaches only log attributes and AgentSession.AgentName. Making it an error would break any out-of-tree plugin that already has one.

Design · 1

Registry entries carry either a factory or an error

In cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go, replacing map[types.AgentName]Factory: 

type entry struct {
    factory Factory // nil when the external binary could not be loaded
    binary  string  // external binaries only; "" for built-ins
    err     error   // non-nil when unusable
}

var registry = make(map[types.AgentName]entry)
  • Register(name, factory) — unchanged signature, stores entry{factory}. Built-in init() registrations are untouched.
  • RegisterExternal(name, binary, factory) — stores a usable external, overwriting any built-in under that name.
  • RegisterExternalFailure(name, binary, err) — stores the failure, overwriting whatever was there. This is the shadowing case.
  • Get(name) — absent entry gives today's unknown agent error; an entry with err != nil returns that error, wrapped as external agent %q (%s) is not usable: %w. Never calls a nil factory.
  • List, StringList, DetectAll, GetByAgentType, LauncherFor, Default — skip factory == nil entries, so those keep meaning "registered and callable".
  • ExternalFailures() — sorted by name, for listing.
  • ProbedExternalBinaries() — the memo source, built from entries with a non-empty binary.
  • ResetExternalsForTesting() — drops every external entry; tests call it via t.Cleanup so the process-wide memo does not leak between tests.

Design · 2

Discovery becomes three phases

A rewrite of discoverAndRegister. The phases run in order, and only the middle one touches a subprocess.

  1. PHASE 01

    Collect

    candidates(ctx) — pure filesystem, no exec. Walk the PATH entries, glob entire-agent-*, skip unreadable dirs, derive each agent name, and drop anything already in the memo. Returns {name, binPath} pairs.

  2. PHASE 02

    Probe

    One goroutine per candidate, each with its own context.WithTimeout(ctx, infoTimeout), reporting on a buffered channel. Inside: os.Stat, then New, then Wrap. Error wrapping is unchanged, so messages stay diagnostic.

  3. PHASE 03

    Register

    The calling goroutine drains the channel and sorts by name for deterministic ordering, then calls RegisterExternal or RegisterExternalFailure per result, logging overrides and name mismatches.

Latent bug this fixes

Today's dedup key is the binary basename, so entire-agent-foo.exe and entire-agent-foo.com in one directory both derive agent foo and the second silently overwrites the first — while PATHEXT picks whichever it likes. The collect phase dedups on the derived agent name instead. First PATH directory wins, matching PATH semantics.

Fan-out is unbounded: the realistic candidate count is single digits, and a cap would serialize exactly the case the parallelism is for.

A single ctx.Err() != nil guard at entry replaces discoveryCanceled/discoveryCtxErr, which are deleted along with discoveryTimeout. Those two helpers exist only to paper over the derived-context-shadowing bug in the old sequential loop; now each probe owns a context derived from the caller, so a cancelled caller cancels every probe and each error already wraps the context error.

discoverAndRegisterNamed keeps its exec.LookPath shape (it honours PATHEXT) and its path-separator rejection, switches to infoTimeout, records failures the same way, and still returns its error to the caller. The statExternalAgent seam is removed; lookPathExternalAgent stays, because one test asserts it is never reached.

Design · 3

entire agent list surfaces broken externals

runAgentList never discovers externals today, so external agents do not appear there at all. Add external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways(ctx) at the top — the Always variant, because a listing command should show what is on PATH regardless of the external_agents setting, the same reasoning runSetupFlow already uses. Then print a section after the existing list whenever agent.ExternalFailures() is non-empty. 

Agents:
  ✓ claude-code
    codex
    roger-roger

Broken external agents:
  ✗ foo  (/usr/local/bin/entire-agent-foo): info: invalid JSON: ...

Tests

Written before the implementation

discovery_test.go is largely rewritten, reusing the existing setupDiscoveryDir, makeInfoJSON, enableExternalAgents and mockInfoScript helpers.

New testAsserts
_RegistersReadyAgents Two good binaries in two PATH dirs are both registered and callable.
_RecordsFailedAgent An invalid-JSON binary is absent from List() and present in ExternalFailures() with its binary path and a diagnostic error; a good binary in the same scan still registers.
_SlowInfoTimesOutWithoutBlockingOthers A sleep 60 binary is recorded as failed with context.DeadlineExceeded, a good binary alongside it registers, and the whole call finishes well under 2 s — proving the probes are parallel and isolated.
_ExternalOverridesBuiltIn A pre-registered built-in factory is replaced by a good same-named external; Get returns the external.
_BrokenExternalShadowsBuiltIn Built-in plus broken same-named external: the name is gone from List/StringList, Get returns the external's error, and the entry appears in ExternalFailures().
_NonExecutableRecordedAsFailure A mode-0644 match becomes a failure entry rather than a silent skip.
_DirectoryRecordedAsFailure A directory named entire-agent-* becomes a failure entry.
_MemoizesReadyAndFailed Binaries that append to a counter file: two DiscoverAndRegisterAlways calls produce exactly one exec each, for a good and a failing binary.
_DedupesOnDerivedAgentName The same derived name in dir A and dir Z resolves to dir A's binary, distinguished by its info.type.
_NameMismatchStillRegisters entire-agent-foo reporting "name": "bar" is registered under foo and is callable.
Existing testsFate
_EmptyPATH, _UnreadableDir, _SkipsWhenDisabled, _Deduplication, TestIsExternal_*, both Windows .bat tests keep They still describe real behaviour.
named: _InvalidInfo, _MissingHelper, _RejectsPathSeparators, _CanceledContext, _TimesOutStalledInfo keep _TimesOutStalledInfo retargeted at 300 ms.
_DeadlineWhileLookingUpMissingHelper, _ReportsCallerDeadlineExpiredDuringLookup (and its bespoke stalledPropagationCtx), _HelperDisappearsAfterLookup, _StatError, _LookPathError delete They pin mechanisms this refactor removes, or inject through seams that are going away.
_SkipsNameConflict delete The behaviour it asserts is now inverted.
_SkipsNonExecutable, _SkipsDirectory delete Replaced by the failure-recording versions above.
registry_test.go add Get on a failure entry returns the recorded error; List/StringList exclude it; GetByAgentType and DetectAll do not panic on a nil factory.
agent_group_test.go add runAgentList output shows a ready external in the normal list and a broken one under Broken external agents: with its reason.

Scope

Files touched

  • cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go + registry_test.go
  • cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery.go + discovery_test.go
  • cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go + agent_group_test.go
  • docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md §Discovery is already stale ("runs once during CLI initialization"); rewrite for lazy, parallel, 300 ms. §Error Handling changes from "the binary is skipped" to "recorded as a broken agent". Document override + shadowing, and add the undocumented ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION env var while in there.
  • docs/architecture/external-commands.md update the DiscoverAndRegisterAlways row (~line 267)

Deliberately untouched: external.go and capabilities.go (New, run, Wrap are unchanged), the settings.IsExternalAgentsEnabled gate on DiscoverAndRegister, and every call site in setup.go / explain_summary_provider.go — the signatures stay identical.

Verification

How we know it works

  1. mise run test — unit tests, including the new discovery, registry and list tests.
  2. mise run test:integration and mise run test:e2e:canary — the canary exercises the hook trees that call DiscoverAndRegister under a 5 s context.
  3. mise run fmt && mise run lint, linting again if fmt rewrote anything. Use the mise-installed golangci-lint directly — a stale v1 shadows it on PATH.
  4. Manual, in a scratch repo: put three binaries on PATH — one good, one printing garbage, one sleep 60 — and check entire agent list shows the good one in the list and the other two under Broken external agents with distinct reasons, returning in well under a second. Then add a good entire-agent-claude-code and confirm the takeover is logged and entire agent add claude-code drives the external.
  5. time entire agent list with the sleep 60 binary present, to confirm the 300 ms bound holds.

Follow-ups

Out of scope

  • Turning an info.name / binary-suffix mismatch into a hard error.
  • Surfacing broken externals in entire status and its --json output.
  • Retuning infoTimeout away from 300 ms once real cold-start numbers exist. macOS Gatekeeper on a first exec of a large Go binary is the case most likely to need it.

320 docs/external-agents/pi-version.md
# External Agent Discovery Refactor — Implementation Plan

Status: fully agreed. Both previously-open decisions are resolved — see
[Resolved decisions](#resolved-decisions).
Scope: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery.go` and its tests.

Read this whole document before writing code.

## Why

`discoverAndRegister` — the shared body behind `DiscoverAndRegister` and
`DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` — executes every `entire-agent-*` binary on `$PATH`
**serially** under one 10s budget, checking for cancellation only *between*
binaries. One slow plugin therefore eats the whole budget and every later
binary is dropped as "timed out". Every failure is `logging.Debug`'d and then
lost, so a plugin that is present but unloadable is indistinguishable from a
plugin that was never installed.

Both matter because the `Always` variant runs on interactive, user-waiting
paths, up to three times per process (see [Idempotency](#idempotency)).

## Target design

### Two registries in `external`

Ready agents keep going into the `agent` registry (so `agent.Get`,
`agent.List`, `hookAgentOptions`, `DetectAll` are unchanged). `external` gains
its own record of both outcomes, for a future "external agent state" listing:

```go
// BrokenAgent is an external agent binary that exists on $PATH but could not
// be loaded.
type BrokenAgent struct {
    Name       types.AgentName
    BinaryPath string
    Err        error
}
```

Package-level state, guarded by one mutex:

- `ready map[types.AgentName]agent.Agent`
- `broken map[types.AgentName]BrokenAgent`

### Idempotency

`entire enable` / bare `entire` with no `--agent` calls `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways`
three times: `setup.go:891` (root/enable `RunE`, so `--agent` resolves),
`setup.go:402` (`runSetupFlow`), `setup.go:496` (`runManageAgents`). They are
defensive, not sequential-by-design — each is independently reachable (bare root,
`entire configure`, `entire enable`, the non-interactive skill path).

Do **not** prune those call sites in this change; auditing every entry point is
separate work. Instead make discovery idempotent per agent name: the scan phase
skips any name already present in `ready` or `broken`. Calls 2 and 3 then cost a
`$PATH` glob and nothing else, and the broken list stops flapping between calls.

Accepted cost: a `chmod +x` performed mid-process is not picked up. The user
re-runs the command.

### Two invariants to preserve

- **A missing binary is not a broken agent.** `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways`
  returns `nil` on `exec.ErrNotFound` — that means "no such plugin, fall
  through to other resolution", and its one production caller
  (`explain_summary_provider.go:57`, the `--summarize-provider` override)
  depends on it. It must not land in `broken` either.
- **The `external_agents` gate stays where it is.** `DiscoverAndRegister`
  checks `settings.IsExternalAgentsEnabled` and returns before scanning;
  `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` does not. Only the shared body changes.

## Resolved decisions

### 1. A built-in always wins a name collision. Log it at `Warn`.

Override was considered and **rejected as a hijack vector**. Keep this rationale
with the code — it is the reason the collision branch must never call `New`.

`agent.Register` overwrites process-wide, and the gated `DiscoverAndRegister`
runs inside `hooks_cmd.go` and `hooks_git_cmd.go`. So dropping
`entire-agent-claude-code` anywhere on `$PATH` — `./node_modules/.bin`, a
`mise`/`asdf` shim dir, any dir ahead of the real one — would silently replace
the built-in agent that reads transcripts and writes checkpoints, on every hook.
Today built-ins are immune *and* the colliding binary is never executed;
override would mean executing it and handing it the session. The same mechanism
shadows `vogon`, breaking the e2e canary in a way that looks like a CLI bug.

So: built-in wins, the binary is **not** executed, and the shadowing attempt is
logged at `Warn` with binary path and agent name — which fixes the original
invisibility complaint without the takeover. A collision produces **no** `broken`
entry; it is not a broken agent.

### 2. `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` drops from 10s to 300ms.

Confirmed. It shares the budget with the scan path. Its only production caller
is the `--summarize-provider` / dispatch override, and that is still just an
`info` call.

## ⚠ The 300ms budget is measured to be too small — read before coding

The requester owns this number and intends to tune it, so it is **not** a
blocker for the refactor. But it was measured, and at 300ms the design does not
work on a cold binary. Do not discover this again from failing tests.

Measured on macOS (Apple silicon), forking a freshly written shell script:

| Case | Time |
| --- | --- |
| First exec in a fresh process, freshly written file | 320–394ms |
| Each further *newly written* file, same process | 140–170ms |
| Re-exec of a file already run once | 7–12ms |
| `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (inside the budget, see below) | ~13ms |

So the cost is dominated by **first exec of a given binary**, not by process
warm-up: on macOS a newly installed binary pays code-signing / Gatekeeper
validation and cold page-in on its first run. Consequences:

- A user who has just installed a plugin gets a `broken` entry with
  `ErrInfoTimeout` on the very first `entire` command, and a working plugin from
  then on. That is the worst possible first impression, and it is intermittent.
- A real plugin is a compiled binary or, worse, a Node/Python wrapper — both
  strictly slower to start than the `sh` script measured above.
- **Every test that writes a mock agent into a fresh `t.TempDir()` hits the cold
  path**, so at 300ms essentially all discovery tests fail. This is not a test
  bug; do not "fix" it by loosening the assertions.
- `Agent.run` additionally calls `paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)`, which can shell out
  to git (~13ms) *inside* the budget, before the plugin is even executed.

Options, for the requester to pick from:

1. **Raise the constant** to ~2s. Still bounded, still parallel, so a scan costs
   ~2s worst case instead of N×2s; a healthy plugin answers in ~10ms and the
   budget is never approached. Simplest, and the one this document assumes if no
   other decision is made.
2. Keep 300ms as the steady-state budget but grant a longer budget on a binary's
   first exec (e.g. keyed by path+mtime in the cache dir). Correct but adds
   persistent state to a discovery path — over-engineered for now.
3. Keep 300ms and accept first-run failure. Not recommended; see above.

Whichever value is chosen, `ErrInfoTimeout` must stay distinguishable from a
genuine load failure — that is what makes a too-tight budget diagnosable instead
of looking like a broken plugin.

## Tests

Tests in `discovery_test.go` modify process-global state (`os.Setenv`,
`t.Chdir`, the agent registry, and the new ready/broken registries) so they
cannot use `t.Parallel()`. Keep that constraint and its existing comment.

Two constraints that will otherwise waste a debugging cycle:

- **Every mock agent written into a fresh `t.TempDir()` is a cold exec** —
  140–400ms on macOS. See the budget section above. Tests that assert a healthy

### Delete

prove a context-shadowing bug the refactor removes by construction:

- `TestDiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways_LookPathError`
- `TestDiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways_HelperDisappearsAfterLookup`
- `TestDiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways_DeadlineWhileLookingUpMissingHelper`
- `TestDiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways_ReportsCallerDeadlineExpiredDuringLookup`
- the `stalledPropagationCtx` type

`discoveryCanceled` / `discoveryCtxErr` helpers, whose whole purpose was
guarding the shadowing bug. Keep the `lookPathExternalAgent` seam —
`TestDiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways_RejectsPathSeparators` uses it to assert we
never look up a name containing a path separator.

### Keep

`_FindsAgent`, `_Deduplication`, `_SkipsNameConflict` (built-in survives, per
decision 1), `_SkipsNonExecutable` (now asserts a `broken` entry, not silence),
`_SkipsDirectory`, `_SkipsWhenDisabled`, `_EmptyPATH`, `_UnreadableDir`,
`_ContinuesAfterRegistrationError`, `_SkipsInfoFailure`,
`Named_{InvalidInfo,MissingHelper,RejectsPathSeparators,TimesOutStalledInfo,CanceledContext}`,
the two Windows `.bat` tests, `TestIsExternal_*`.

Realistic behaviour only — no mock-seam tests.

1. **Parallelism.** Put four binaries that `sleep` past the budget on `$PATH`
   alongside one that answers. Assert the fast one registers, the slow ones land
   in `broken`, and total elapsed time is far below `4×infoTimeout`. Use four
   rather than one: with a single slow binary, serial and concurrent execution
   differ by only one budget, which is not a gap you can assert on reliably. This
   is the regression the refactor exists to prevent.

between them and make failures order-dependent.

```bash

```

  `explain_summary_provider.go:30`, `e2e/testutil/session_paths.go:26`

The gated path running in hooks is why [decision 1](#resolved-decisions) went
the way it did. Signature changes are not planned, so no call site should need

## Documentation

`docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md` describes the discovery contract.

# Refactor external agent discovery: parallel, strictly-bounded, state-recording

**Deliverable of this planning turn:** write this up as
`docs/external-agents/claude-version.md`, alongside the existing
`docs/external-agents/pi-version.md`, so the two plans can be compared on the same facts.
No code in this turn.

## Context

`external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery.go`) scans `$PATH`
for `entire-agent-*` binaries, execs each one's `info` subcommand, and registers the result in the
agent registry. Two problems:

1. **Sequential.** Binaries are exec'd one at a time inside a single 10s budget checked only
   *between* binaries. A hung binary is bounded instead by `external.defaultRunTimeout` (30s), so a
   scan can overrun its own cap by ~30s. Both hook call sites (`hooks_cmd.go:48`,
   `hooks_git_cmd.go:177`) wrap it in a 5s context a single slow plugin blows through.
2. **Failures vanish.** `discoverAndRegister` returns nothing. Bad JSON, protocol mismatch,
   non-zero exit, missing exec bit, timeout — all go to `logging.Debug` and the loop moves on. A
   user whose plugin does not appear has no way to find out why.

## Decisions (final)

- **Per-binary timeout is 300ms**, provisional and owned by the requester. The measured cold-exec
  numbers below say it is too small; the doc records them rather than quietly changing the number.
- **Everything unusable is an error entry**: exec failure, timeout, invalid JSON, protocol
  mismatch, `Wrap` failure, missing exec bit, and a glob match that is a directory. A *missing*
  binary is not a broken agent (`DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` must keep returning nil on
  `exec.ErrNotFound` — `explain_summary_provider.go` depends on that meaning "fall through").
- **A built-in always wins a name collision.** The colliding binary is never executed; the attempt
  is logged at `Warn` (today it is `Debug`, which is why it was invisible). It produces **no** error
  entry — it is not a broken agent. Rationale to keep with the code: the gated
  `DiscoverAndRegister` runs inside the hook trees, so an override would let
  `entire-agent-claude-code` dropped into any `$PATH` dir take over transcript reads and checkpoint
  writes on every hook, and shadow `vogon` in a way that looks like a CLI bug.
- **Memoized per process**: a binary already probed — ready or failed — is not re-exec'd. Keyed by
  binary path. One setup flow calls `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` up to four times today. Accepted
  cost: a mid-process `chmod +x` is not picked up; the user re-runs the command.
- **State lives in the agent registry** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go`).
- **`info.name` mismatching the binary suffix stays working** (registers under the binary-derived
  name) plus a warning log. It is cosmetic: every resolution path keys off the registry name, never
  `Agent.Name()` — the mismatch reaches only log attributes and `AgentSession.AgentName`
  (`resume.go:1048`). Making it an error would break any out-of-tree plugin that has one.
- **Timeout stays classifiable.** `cmd.Run` reports only `signal: killed` when the context kills the
  child, so export `ErrInfoTimeout` (joined with the context error so
  `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` also holds) and `ErrNotExecutable`. This is what makes
  a too-tight budget diagnosable instead of looking like a broken plugin.

### The 300ms budget is measured to be too small — record, don't hide

Measured on macOS (Apple silicon), forking a freshly written shell script:

| Case | Time |
| --- | --- |
| First exec in a fresh process, freshly written file | 320–394ms |
| Each further newly-written file, same process | 140–170ms |
| Re-exec of a file already run once | 7–12ms |
| `paths.WorktreeRoot` shelling out to git, *inside* the budget | ~13ms |

Cost is dominated by **first exec of a given binary** (code-signing / Gatekeeper validation, cold
page-in), not process warm-up. So: a freshly installed plugin fails once, intermittently, on the
user's first `entire` command; a real plugin (compiled Go, or a Node/Python wrapper) is strictly
slower than the `sh` script measured; and **every test writing a mock agent into a fresh
`t.TempDir()` is a cold exec**, so discovery tests must override the constant rather than have
their assertions loosened.

## Design

### 1. Registry entries carry either a factory or an error

`cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go`, replacing `map[types.AgentName]Factory`:

```go
type entry struct {
    factory Factory // nil when the external binary could not be loaded
    binary  string  // external binaries only; "" for built-ins
    err     error   // non-nil when unusable
}
var registry = make(map[types.AgentName]entry)
```

Because a built-in always wins a collision, a failure entry can never displace a working built-in —
so failures can safely share the name-keyed map.

- `Register(name, factory)` — unchanged signature, stores `entry{factory}`. Built-in `init()`
  registrations untouched.
- `RegisterExternal(name, binary, factory)` / `RegisterExternalFailure(name, binary, err)`.
- `Get(name)` — absent → today's `unknown agent` error; `err != nil` → that error, wrapped
  `external agent %q (%s) is not usable: %w`. Never calls a nil factory.
- `List`, `StringList`, `DetectAll`, `GetByAgentType`, `LauncherFor`, `Default` — skip
  `factory == nil`, so they keep meaning "registered and callable".
- `ExternalFailures()` — sorted snapshot (a copy, never the live map) for listing.
- `ProbedExternalBinaries()` — the memo source, from entries with a non-empty `binary`.
- `ResetExternalsForTesting()` — drops every external entry; tests call it via `t.Cleanup` so the
  process-wide memo does not leak and make failures order-dependent.

### 2. Discovery becomes collect → probe → register

**Collect** (`candidates(ctx)`) — pure filesystem, no exec. Walk `filepath.SplitList(PATH)`, glob
`entire-agent-*`, skip unreadable dirs. Derive the name via `StripExeExt` + `TrimPrefix` and **dedup
on the derived agent name, not the basename** — today's basename dedup lets `foo.exe` and `foo.com`
in one dir both derive agent `foo` and silently race while PATHEXT picks one. First PATH dir wins.
Skip names colliding with a registered agent (Warn, no exec) and binaries already in
`ProbedExternalBinaries()`. `os.Stat` here too: directory or missing exec bit → failure entry
recorded without spawning a goroutine.

**Probe** — one goroutine per surviving candidate, each with its own
`context.WithTimeout(ctx, infoTimeout)` derived from the caller, so a tighter caller deadline still
wins and total wall time is ~one budget rather than N×budget. Inside: `New(ctx, binPath)`, then
`Wrap(ea)`. Results go on a buffered channel; goroutines never register. Unbounded fan-out — the
realistic candidate count is single digits, and a cap would serialize the very case the parallelism
is for. If the caller context is already done, skip exec entirely and record every candidate with
the context error.

**Register** — the calling goroutine drains the channel, applies results in scan order (so
registration is deterministic), and logs overrides and name mismatches.

`discoveryTimeout`, `discoveryCanceled`, `discoveryCtxErr` and the `statExternalAgent` seam are all
deleted; a single `ctx.Err()` guard at entry replaces the two helpers, whose only purpose was
guarding the derived-context-shadowing bug the new shape removes by construction.
`lookPathExternalAgent` stays — `_RejectsPathSeparators` asserts it is never reached.

`discoverAndRegisterNamed` keeps `exec.LookPath` (it honours PATHEXT) and its path-separator
rejection, switches to `infoTimeout`, records failures the same way, and still returns its error.

### 3. `entire agent list` surfaces broken externals

`runAgentList` (`cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go`) never discovers externals today, so they do not
appear there at all. Add `external.DiscoverAndRegisterAlways(ctx)` at the top — the `Always`
variant, because a listing command should show what is on `PATH` regardless of the
`external_agents` setting, the same reasoning `runSetupFlow` uses — then print a section when
`agent.ExternalFailures()` is non-empty:

```
Broken external agents:
  ✗ foo  (/usr/local/bin/entire-agent-foo): info: invalid JSON: ...
```

## Tests

Written before the implementation. `discovery_test.go` keeps its no-`t.Parallel()` constraint and
comment (it mutates `os.Setenv`, `t.Chdir`, and global registries). Reuse `setupDiscoveryDir`,
`makeInfoJSON`, `enableExternalAgents`, `mockInfoScript`. Every test resets externals via
`t.Cleanup`, and any test that execs a mock overrides `infoTimeout` — a fresh `t.TempDir()` binary
is a cold exec (see the measured table).

**Keep:** `_FindsAgent`, `_Deduplication`, `_SkipsNameConflict` (built-in survives — now also
asserts the Warn and that the binary was never executed), `_SkipsWhenDisabled`, `_EmptyPATH`,
`_UnreadableDir`, `_ContinuesAfterRegistrationError`, `_SkipsInfoFailure`, `TestIsExternal_*`, both
Windows `.bat` tests, and named `_InvalidInfo`, `_MissingHelper`, `_RejectsPathSeparators`,
`_CanceledContext`, `_TimesOutStalledInfo`.

**Delete** — mechanisms this refactor removes, or seam-injection: `_StatError`, `_LookPathError`,
`_HelperDisappearsAfterLookup`, `_DeadlineWhileLookingUpMissingHelper`,
`_ReportsCallerDeadlineExpiredDuringLookup` and its `stalledPropagationCtx` type. `_SkipsNonExecutable`
and `_SkipsDirectory` are rewritten to assert a failure entry rather than silence.

**Add:**

| Test | Asserts |
| --- | --- |
| `_ParallelProbesDoNotSerialize` | four `sleep`-past-budget binaries plus one good one: the good one registers, the slow ones are broken, elapsed is far below 4×budget. Four rather than one — with a single slow binary, serial and parallel differ by one budget, which is not reliably assertable. This is the regression the refactor exists to prevent. |
| `_TimeoutIsClassifiable` | the stalled entry satisfies `errors.Is(err, ErrInfoTimeout)` and `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` |
| `_NonExecutableIsClassifiable` | `errors.Is(err, ErrNotExecutable)` |
| `_DirectoryRecordedAsFailure` | a directory named `entire-agent-*` becomes a failure entry |
| `_RecordsFailedAgent` | invalid-JSON binary absent from `List()`, present in `ExternalFailures()` with its path and a diagnostic error; a good binary in the same scan still registers |
| `_AlreadyCancelledCallerExecsNothing` | every candidate recorded broken with the context error, and non-execution asserted observably (a binary that would drop a marker file) |
| `_MemoizesReadyAndFailed` | two consecutive calls: marker-file count stays 1 for a good *and* a failing binary; snapshots unchanged |
| `_DedupesOnDerivedAgentName` | same derived name in dir A and dir Z → dir A's binary wins, distinguished by its `info.type` |
| `_NameMismatchStillRegisters` | `entire-agent-foo` reporting `"name": "bar"` registers under `foo` and is callable |

`registry_test.go`: `Get` on a failure entry returns the recorded error; `List`/`StringList` exclude
it; `GetByAgentType` and `DetectAll` do not panic on a nil factory.

`agent_group_test.go`: `runAgentList` shows a ready external in the normal list and a broken one
under `Broken external agents:` with its reason.

## Files touched

- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/registry.go` (+ `registry_test.go`)
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/external/discovery.go` (+ `discovery_test.go`)
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent_group.go` (+ `agent_group_test.go`)
- `docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md` — §Discovery is stale ("runs once during CLI
  initialization"); rewrite for lazy, parallel, per-binary budget. §Error Handling changes from "the
  binary is skipped" to "recorded as a broken agent and shown by `entire agent list`". Note the Warn
  on a collision, and add the undocumented `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION` env var while in there.
- `docs/architecture/external-commands.md` — update the `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` row (~line 267).

Untouched: `external.go` / `capabilities.go` (`New`, `run`, `Wrap` unchanged), the
`settings.IsExternalAgentsEnabled` gate on `DiscoverAndRegister`, and every call site — signatures
stay identical.

## Verification

1. `mise run test` — unit tests, including the new discovery/registry/list tests.
2. `mise run test:integration` and `mise run test:e2e:canary` (external discovery runs in
   `e2e/testutil`, and the canary exercises the hook trees under a 5s context).
3. `mise run fmt && mise run lint`, re-linting if `fmt` rewrote anything. Use the mise-installed
   `golangci-lint` directly — a stale v1 shadows it on PATH.
4. Manual, in a scratch repo: one good binary, one printing garbage, one `sleep 60` on `$PATH` —
   `entire agent list` shows the good one in the list and the other two under *Broken external
   agents* with distinct reasons, returning fast. Then add a good `entire-agent-claude-code` and
   confirm the built-in still wins, with a Warn naming the shadowing binary.
5. `time entire agent list` with the `sleep 60` binary present, to confirm the budget holds.

## Out of scope

- Retuning `infoTimeout` (owned by the requester; the measured table is the input).
- Turning an `info.name` / binary-suffix mismatch into a hard error.
- Surfacing broken externals in `entire status` / `--json`.
- Pruning the redundant `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways` call sites in `setup.go` — auditing every entry
  point is separate work; memoization makes the extra calls nearly free.
